text:
Plant communities on approximately 25,000 acres of reclaimed area will reflect the altered soil characteristics, and it is unlikely that native plant communities can ever be duplicated.
Wildlife resources that are irretrievably lost include individual animals and habitats that are destroyed. Animals and plants that would have reproduced in the affected habitats during the life of the mining operation will be irretrievably lost. Most wildlife losses may be reversible if the species and habitat are not impacted to the point that their ability to reproduce is seriously impaired. Five grouse dancing grounds (leks) on Tracts III and two on Tract II constitute special areas to these birds and are used year after year. Destruction of those leks may result in the permanent loss of grouse breeding areas on the reclaimed lands.
During the life of the operation, approximately 25,000 acres will be mined. Agricultural production will be foregone irretrievably while the land is involved in active mining and reclamation activities. This time period is expected to be at least seven years at a given location. Hence, over the life of the operation, about 5,586 animal units of cumulative grazing capacity and an estimated $483,000 of income from cropland would be irretrievably lost. Agricultural land committed to residential use will be permanently lost.
Where possible, existing timber resources on 8,630 acres will be harvested prior to mining. However, timber volume in immature trees and their potential maturation into harvestable timber will be lost.
If any archaeological sites are not discovered prior to mining, their loss will be a permanent irreversible commitment of resources.
